title: Multimodal Tokenization, Patches & Resamplers
interviewAnswer: Text becomes discrete tokens, while images are usually represented as patches or learned visual features. A multimodal model must convert those features into a manageable token sequence—often through patch embeddings, pooling, learned queries, a Q-Former or a Perceiver-style resampler—before the language model consumes them.
why: Token count is one of the main accuracy/latency/memory trade-offs in VLM inference.
intuition: A 4K image contains far too many pixels to treat each pixel like a word. Convert it into a much smaller set of semantic visual tokens.
deepDive: ViT-style encoders patchify the image and produce contextual features. Some systems pass many patch features to the LLM; others use learned queries/resamplers to compress them. High-resolution strategies may tile/crop images, which improves fine detail but multiplies visual tokens and prefill cost.
workedExample: A 336×336 image with 14×14 patches gives 24×24=576 patch positions before any pooling/resampling.
commonMistakes: Calling visual patch embeddings “the same tokenizer” as BPE text tokens.
Ignoring the quadratic or memory cost of injecting many visual tokens.
followUps: How would you handle high-resolution documents?
production: Benchmark quality versus visual-token count and resolution; cache or reuse visual embeddings for repeated questions about the same image.
